Dave started with an unknown number of fries. He ate 14, leaving \(x - 14\). The seagull ate half of what Dave ate, which is 7, leaving \(x - 21\). Three pigeons ate 3 fries each (9 total), leaving \(x - 30\). A raccoon stole two-thirds of the remaining fries, so one-third remained: \(\frac{1}{3}(x - 30)\). Ants carried off 1 fry, leaving 5. This gives the equation:
\[
\frac{1}{3}(x - 30) - 1 = 5
\]
\[
\frac{1}{3}(x - 30) = 6
\]
\[
x - 30 = 18
\]
\[
x = 48
\]
Checking: 48 - 14 = 34; 34 - 7 = 27; 27 - 9 = 18; raccoon takes 12, leaving 6; ants take 1, leaving 5. The solution is consistent.

Answer: 48
